newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures end up but below peaks after FOMC.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures end up but below peaks after FOMC.

text.p: The Fed's decision Tuesday to keep U.S. interest rates unchanged left U.S. debt futures moderately higher but well below session peaks.
Even before the Federal Open Market Committee meeting ended, futures had begun grinding upward as 1315 CDT/1815 GMT approached and no announcement came out of the meeting.
On the ensuing rally, December Treasury bonds and Eurodollars matched their Sept 13 peaks at 109-00 and 94.20, respectively, before stalling and backing off again.
"But it was really thin in there," said a T-bond futures floor broker. "Nobody was really stepping up to do anything."
The short end of the market outperformed the long end, with December Euros again challenging 94.20 near the close as buyers resurfaced.

"They got frustrated and it got pretty weak five or eight minutes before the close but then it closed pretty strong," said a Eurodollar floor broker. "We could shoot for 94.25 in the December (contract)."
Traders said the excitment about no change in rates overshadowed subsequent news that weekly Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales fell 0.3 percent.
"We were swamped," said the bond broker. "I didn't see it."
Another T-bond broker said little trading occurred around the day's high at 109-00, where activity was thin and extremely choppy.

He noted that some hedge funds were seen buying heavily during the morning below 108-00 and that some of them may have evened up when the rally stalled, with many analysts still thinking the Fed may tighten by the end of the year.
He also said dealers were leery of being too long of paper before this week's two- and five-year Treasury note auctions.
"They (Fed) still have a bias to tighten, and they have to issue debt," he said.

At settlement, December T-bonds were up 17/23 at 108-20/32, T-notes added 13/32 to 106-30/32, munis gained 17/32 to 113-20/32, T-bills rose 12 basis points to 94.74 and Eurodollars gained 12 basis points to 94.18. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
